title: Affine Artin-type bound for the constructible weak Serre coproduct class over a profinite geometric base
statement:
Fix a prime $\ell$, an algebraic closure $\Omega=\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$, a finite subextension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$, and a finite commutative ring $A$ killed by a power of $\ell$. Let $\Lambda\in\{A,\mathbf Z_\ell,\mathcal O_E,\mathbf Q_\ell,E,\Omega\}$, with the discrete topology for $A$ and the induced $\ell$-adic topology otherwise [sk-def-localizing-closure]. Its condensed ring uses all continuous maps from profinite sets, including when $\Lambda=\Omega$. For a scheme $T$ put $\Lambda_T=p_T^*\Lambda$ and $\mathcal A_T=\operatorname{Mod}_{\Lambda_T}$, using ordinary uncompleted module-object derived categories [sk-def-sfb-module-derived-pushpull] and the small-site/indexing universe [def-weil-size-convention]. Let $\mathcal P_T$ be the intersection of all replete classes in $\mathcal A_T$ containing zero and all finite constant scalar-model constructible modules [sk-def-sfb-constructible], closed under kernels and cokernels of maps between members, extensions, and all small ambient coproducts. Extension closure means that in $0\to M'\to M\to M''\to0$ membership of both ends implies membership of the middle. 
Let $C$ be an affine reduced zero-dimensional w-contractible scheme whose residue fields are separably closed [sk-def-pe-wlocal]; zero-dimensional means that every prime of its affine coordinate ring is maximal. Let $g:U\to C$ be a finite-type morphism with $U$ affine [def-pc-scheme, def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. Let $e\geq0$ be an integer, and assume that for every geometric point $\bar c:\operatorname{Spec}K\to C$ with $K$ algebraically closed, the fibre $U_{\bar c}=U\times_C\operatorname{Spec}K$ has topological Krull dimension at most $e$ [def-weil-geometric-fibre, def-kun-topological-krull-dimension]. Then for every $N\in\mathcal P_U$ and every integer $q>e+2$,
$$H^q\bigl(R\Gamma(U_{\mathrm{pro\acute et}},N)\bigr)=0.$$
Here $R\Gamma$ is right-derived global sections of the ordinary internal $\Lambda_U$-module category with values in $D(\mathbf{Ab})$, and $N$ is in degree zero. No properness, Noetherianity, finite presentation of $g$, invertibility of $\ell$, completeness of $N$, or finite-subextension-valued replacement of the norm topology on $\Omega$ is assumed. Empty schemes and zero-dimensional fibres are included.

proof.text: Write $R=\Gamma(C,\mathcal O_C)$. For $c\in C$, every prime of $R$ is maximal, so $R_c$ has only one prime, its maximal ideal. Localization preserves reducedness: if $(a/s)^n=0$, choose $t\notin c$ with $ta^n=0$; then $(ta)^n=0$, hence $ta=0$, hence $a/s=0$. Thus the nilradical of $R_c$ is zero; as it is also the unique prime ideal, the maximal ideal is zero. Consequently $R_c=\kappa(c)$ is a separably closed field. The algebraic strict henselization of a separably closed field is the field itself: by the equivalence between étale schemes over a field and discrete Galois sets, every pointed étale algebra has its selected factor equal to that field, and localization at the selected point gives the field. These selected-factor maps give the colimit in the definition of strict henselization. The affine strict-local comparison therefore identifies $C_{(\bar c)}$ over $C$ with $\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(c)$ for a geometric point defined using an algebraic closure of $\kappa(c)$. This uses separable closure, not an identification of an imperfect separably closed field with its algebraic closure.

source.place: Tag 03Q9, theorem-higher-direct-images, strict-local base; elementary reduced zero-dimensional local-ring calculation followed by the pointed-étale colimit identification

proof.text: Fix an affine étale test object $v:V\to U$. Both schemes are affine. The étale ring-map lemma makes its coordinate algebra finite type over that of $U$, so $h=gv:V\to C$ is finite type. For each algebraically closed geometric point $\bar c$, $V_{\bar c}\to U_{\bar c}$ is étale. The equality of dimensions of local rings under an étale map implies $\dim V_{\bar c}\leq\dim U_{\bar c}\leq e$: any prime chain in the affine source lies in the localization at its largest prime, whose dimension equals the corresponding target localization. This argument does not require surjectivity of $v$. Affineness also makes $h$ quasi-compact and separated, hence quasi-separated, as required for the strict-henselization stalk formula.

source.place: Tag 07QP, lemma-dimension-etale-extension; finite-type composition and base change on affine coordinate rings

proof.text: For every $c\in C$ put $k_c=\kappa(c)$ and choose an algebraic closure $\overline{k_c}$. The ordinary fibre $V_c$ is affine of finite type over $k_c$. Invariance of dimension under field extension gives $\dim V_c=\dim V_{\overline{k_c}}\leq e$ by Step 2. The field $k_c$ is separably closed, so its torsion étale cohomological dimension is zero. The affine torsion theorem applied to $V_c/k_c$ therefore gives $H^q((V_c)_{\mathrm{et}},G)=0$ for every torsion abelian étale sheaf $G$ and every $q>e$. Its separate empty-scheme clause covers an empty fibre.

Let $F$ be an arbitrary torsion abelian étale sheaf on $V$. For each $c$ and a geometric point over it, the strict-henselization stalk formula for the quasi-compact quasi-separated $h$ gives
$$(R^qh_*F)_{\bar c}\cong H^q((V\times_C C_{(\bar c)})_{\mathrm{et}},F|).$$
Step 1 identifies this strict-local scheme with $V_c$, and inverse image preserves local torsion. Thus Step 3 makes every such stalk zero for $q>e$. Conservativity of geometric stalks applied to $0\to R^qh_*F$ yields $R^qh_*F=0$. There is one chosen geometric point over every point of $C$, and changing its algebraically closed target does not change the strict-local construction.

source.place: Tag 03Q9, theorem-higher-direct-images, applied to h:V→C; étale geometric stalk detection

proof.text:
All points of $C$ are closed and its residue fields are separably closed. The affine zero-dimensional étale acyclicity lemma applies to every abelian sheaf on $C$, and in particular makes global sections exact: for a surjection the obstruction to lifting a global section lies in $H^1$ of its kernel, which vanishes. The exact-global-sections Leray identification now gives
$$H^q(V_{\mathrm{et}},F)\cong\Gamma(C_{\mathrm{et}},R^qh_*F)=0\qquad(q>e).$$
Together with Steps 2–4 this proves the uniform torsion bound on every affine étale $V\to U$ and every torsion $F$, without assuming finite presentation of $U\to C$ or properness.

Apply the topological-coefficient torsion-dimension transfer with $X=U$ and $d=e$. The preceding steps establish exactly its hypothesis for every affine étale test object and every locally torsion abelian étale sheaf. Its coefficient choices, induced norm topology on $\Omega$, internal uncompleted module category, indexing universe, finite constant scalar-model generators and all four weak-Serre/coproduct closure operations are identical to those in the item. Hence its class $\mathcal P_X$ is precisely $\mathcal P_U$, and it gives $H^qR\Gamma(U_{\mathrm{pro\acute et}},N[0])=0$ for every $N\in\mathcal P_U$ and $q>e+2$. This last input is an unsplit coefficient theorem, with its exact source explicitly WANTED; the torsion theorem is not being applied directly to a non-torsion module. The transfer includes the empty scheme and the zero coefficient ring.

Step 1: R_c is a reduced ring with a single prime, so it is the field kappa(c); the pair (kappa(c), id) is terminal in the pointed-etale category, so the strict henselization is kappa(c); the affine comparison lemma gives C_(c) -> C = Spec kappa(c) -> C. Step 2: the etale ring map is of finite type; lem-sc-etale-local-dimension bounds every prime chain of the affine V_cbar by e without needing surjectivity; h is affine, hence qcqs. Step 3: dimension is invariant under field extension, the residue field has torsion cd 0, and the affine torsion theorem applies to V_c (with its empty clause). Steps 4-5: the stalk formula's hypotheses (qcqs h, torsion F) hold, conservativity at one geometric point per point gives R^q h_* F = 0, lem-cbc-affine-sepclosed-etale-acyclic makes global sections on C exact without Noetherianity, and the exact-sections Leray node gives H^q(V,F) = 0 for q > e and every affine etale V. Step 6 applies the new node with X = U and d = e; its coefficients, topologies, generators and closure operations match the item's word for word. proof_deps equals the union of the uses. The new node carries a statement only, is self-contained, and its stmt_deps exist. It is not a relabelling (D1/D2): it has no geometric family, no base and no fibre hypothesis, and the geometric work stays in Steps 1-5. My rg search over dag/nodes (weak-Serre and torsion-cd nodes) found no duplicate; the closest are lem-sfb-higher-direct-image-affine-etale-bound, -zero-dimensional-base-affine-global, -noetherian-proper-heart-uniform-bound, -integral-proper-cohomological-bounds, -finite-classical-localizing and -etale-module-affine-bound. Edge cases: A = 0 and empty X are vacuous; a separably closed point is w-contractible; for finite A everything is classical and the bound is d; for Spec F_q with Z_ell coefficients the bound is d+1 = 2 < 4 (the claim is q > d+2). I found no counterexample. Its source is honestly marked WANTED, and the report avoids the false shortcut that a vanishing class is closed under kernels.
